business_model.claim: Donnelley Financial Solutions, Inc. (DFIN) provides compliance and regulatory software, technology-enabled services, and print and distribution solutions for regulatory filing and deal needs.
quotes: The Company provides regulatory filing and deal solutions via its software, technology-enabled services and print and distribution solutions to public and private companies, mutual funds and other regulated investment firms, to serve its clients’ regulatory and compliance needs.

business_model.claim: DFIN's software solutions consist of ActiveDisclosure, Arc Suite, and Venue, its tech-enabled services cover document composition, SEC EDGAR filing, and transactional solutions, and its print and distribution offerings cover conventional and digital printed products and shipping.
quotes: The Company’s software solutions consist of ActiveDisclosure, Arc Suite and Venue.
The Company’s tech-enabled services offerings consist of document composition, compliance-related SEC EDGAR filing services and transactional solutions.
The Company’s print and distribution offerings primarily consist of conventional and digital printed products and related shipping.

business_model.claim: In 2025, total net sales were $767.0 million, consisting of $358.4 million from software solutions, $298.3 million from tech-enabled services, and $110.3 million from print and distribution.
quotes: Net sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $14.9 million, or 1.9%, to $767.0 million from $781.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, including a $0.8 million, or 0.1%, increase due to changes in foreign currency exchange rates.
Net sales of software solutions of $358.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $28.7 million, or 8.7%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.
Net sales of tech-enabled services of $298.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased $22.5 million, or 7.0%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.
Net sales of print and distribution of $110.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased $21.1 million, or 16.1%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

business_model.claim: In the third quarter of 2026, total net sales were $185.0 million, and software solutions net sales of $95.2 million accounted for 51.5% of total net sales.
quotes: Total net sales of $185.0 million, an increase of $9.7 million, or 5.5%, from the third quarter of 2025.
Software solutions net sales of $95.2 million, an increase of 5.0% from the third quarter of 2025; Software solutions net sales accounted for 51.5% of total net sales.

business_model.claim: DFIN serves public and private companies primarily in North America, Europe, and Asia for capital markets transactions (including IPOs, secondary offerings, M&A, debt offerings, and spinouts) and ongoing Exchange Act compliance filings.
quotes: The Company provides software solutions, tech-enabled services and print and distribution solutions to public and private companies for deal solutions and compliance to companies that are, or are preparing to become, subject to the filing and reporting requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”) and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”).
The Company supports clients primarily in North America, Europe and Asia.

The Company assists its capital markets clients throughout the course of initial public offerings (“IPOs”), secondary offerings, mergers and acquisitions (“M&A”), public and private debt offerings, leveraged buyouts, spinouts, special purpose acquisition companies (“SPAC”) and subsequent de-SPAC transactions and other similar transactions.

In addition, the Company provides clients with compliance solutions to prepare their ongoing required Exchange Act filings that are compatible with the SEC’s EDGAR system, most notably Form 10-K, Form 10-Q, Form 8-K and proxy filings.

business_model.claim: DFIN serves investment company clients—primarily mutual fund companies, alternative investment companies, insurance companies, and third-party fund administrators—in the United States, Europe, and Canada for regulatory reporting and investor communications.
quotes: The Company provides software solutions, tech-enabled services and print and distribution solutions to its investment companies clients, which are primarily mutual fund companies, alternative investment companies, insurance companies and third-party fund administrators, that are subject to the filing and reporting requirements of the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the “Investment Company Act”) as well as European and Canadian regulations.
The Company’s services and sales teams currently support clients in the United States, Europe and Canada.

business_model.claim: Within Capital Markets, the CM-SS segment provides Venue and ActiveDisclosure subscriptions and related services, while the CM-CCM segment provides tech-enabled services and print and distribution solutions for deal and SEC compliance needs.
quotes: Capital Markets – Software Solutions—The CM-SS segment provides Venue and ActiveDisclosure subscriptions and related services (including service packages and services the Company performs on behalf of its clients with customer-facing software) to public and private companies to help manage public and private transactional and compliance processes; collaborate; and tag, validate and file SEC documents.

Capital Markets – Compliance & Communications Management—The CM-CCM segment provides tech-enabled services and print and distribution solutions to public and private companies for deal solutions and SEC compliance requirements.

business_model.claim: Within Investment Companies, the IC-SS segment provides the Arc Suite platform (ArcDigital, ArcPro, ArcRegulatory, and ArcReporting) and related services, the IC-CCM segment provides tech-enabled services, print and distribution, and turnkey proxy services, and Corporate holds unallocated SG&A and benefit-plan items.
quotes: Investment Companies – Software Solutions—The IC-SS segment provides clients with the Arc Suite platform that contains a comprehensive suite of cloud-based solutions, including subscriptions to ArcDigital, ArcPro, ArcRegulatory and ArcReporting as well as related services that enable storage and management of compliance and regulatory information in a self-service, central repository so that documents can be easily accessed, assembled, edited, tagged, translated, rendered and submitted to regulators and investors.

Investment Companies – Compliance & Communications Management—The IC-CCM segment provides clients with tech-enabled services and print and distribution solutions for creating, filing and distributing regulatory communications and solutions for investor communications, as well as iXBRL-formatted filings pursuant to the Investment Company Act, through the SEC’s EDGAR system.

The IC-CCM segment also provides turnkey proxy services, including discovery, planning and implementation, print and mail management, solicitation, tabulation services, stockholder meeting review and expert support.

Corporate is not an operating segment and consists primarily of unallocated selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) activities and associated expenses including, in part, executive, legal, finance and certain facility costs.

business_model.claim: In 2025, segment net sales and Segment Adjusted EBITDA were $230.0 million and $75.0 million for CM-SS, $296.2 million and $113.8 million for CM-CCM, $128.4 million and $50.3 million for IC-SS, and $112.4 million and $39.6 million for IC-CCM, with $38.9 million of Corporate unallocated expenses.
quotes: Net sales of $230.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $16.4 million, or 7.7%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, due to higher ActiveDisclosure net sales of $12.7 million and higher Venue net sales of $3.7 million, both primarily due to increased volumes.

Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $75.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $11.5 million, or 18.1%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to higher net sales of $16.4 million, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses of $4.5 million, largely driven by higher selling expense and higher bad debt expense of $1.1 million, partially offset by cost control initiatives.

Net sales of $296.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased $25.5 million, or 7.9%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to lower tech-enabled services net sales of $18.4 million, driven by a decline in both compliance and transactional volumes, and lower print and distribution net sales of $7.1 million, primarily driven by a decline in compliance volumes.

Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $113.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $2.9 million, or 2.6%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to lower SG&A expenses of $19.6 million and lower cost of sales of $9.0 million, partially offset by lower net sales of $25.5 million.

Net sales of $128.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $12.3 million, or 10.6%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, due to higher non-TSR-related net sales of $6.5 million, largely driven by price increases, and higher net sales of $5.8 million from the Company’s TSR offering, primarily within ArcReporting and ArcDigital.

Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $50.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $10.6 million, or 26.7%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to higher net sales of $12.3 million, partially offset by higher cost of sales of $3.5 million, largely driven by higher product development costs of $1.4 million and higher sales volumes.

Net sales of $112.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased $18.1 million, or 13.9%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to lower print and distribution net sales of $14.0 million, largely driven by a decline in compliance volumes.

Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $39.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased $1.9 million, or 4.6%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to lower net sales of $18.1 million, partially offset by lower cost of sales of $12.4 million, largely driven by lower sales volumes and a lower allocation of overhead costs.

Corporate unallocated expenses of $38.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $0.6 million as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to higher healthcare expense of $1.8 million and higher consulting expense of $1.4 million, partially offset by lower incentive compensation expense.

business_model.claim: Client workflows are shifting toward software solutions combined with tech-enabled services and away from physical print and distribution, except where print is required by regulation or requested by clients.
quotes: The prevailing trend is toward clients choosing to utilize the Company’s software solutions, in conjunction with its tech-enabled services, to meet their document and filing needs, while at the same time shifting away from physical print and distribution of documents, except for when it is still regulatorily required or requested by clients.

Technological advancements, regulatory changes, and evolving workflow preferences have led to the Company’s clients managing more of the financial disclosure process themselves, changing the marketplace for the Company’s services and products.

business_model.claim: SEC regulatory changes—such as requirements for structured, machine-readable data, layered website disclosures, and Tailored Shareholder Reporting (TSR)—enable new software functionality and accelerate the transition from print to software.
quotes: As the regulatory environment continues to evolve, regulators are also demanding a greater use of structured, machine-readable data in companies’ disclosures, more summary documents and layered website disclosures.

Regulatory changes have enabled the Company to offer new value-added functionality and services, leverage its domain expertise and accelerate its transition from print and distribution to software solutions.

business_model.claim: Demand for Capital Markets transactional and Venue offerings depends heavily on global IPO, secondary offering, M&A, debt, and SPAC deal volumes, causing uneven period-to-period revenue.
quotes: The Company’s Capital Markets segments (CM-SS and CM-CCM), in particular, are subject to market volatility, as the demand for the transactional and Venue offerings is largely dependent on the global market for initial public offerings (“IPOs”), secondary offerings, mergers and acquisitions (“M&A”), public and private debt offerings, leveraged buyouts, spinouts, special purpose acquisition company (“SPAC”) and de-SPAC transactions and other similar transactions.
Recently, U.S. capital market transactions, especially IPO and M&A transactions, were disrupted by the U.S. federal government shutdowns that occurred during the fourth quarter of 2025.

The Company’s overall risk profile is balanced by offering services in higher demand during a down market, such as document management tools for the bankruptcy/restructuring process and by moving upstream in the transactional process with products like Venue.

business_model.claim: Investment company revenue is also affected by money inflows and outflows in investment management funds, which determine how many new funds open and close.
quotes: Furthermore, the Company’s offerings for investment companies clients can be affected by fluctuations in the inflow and outflow of money into investment management funds which determines the number of new funds that are opened and closed.

business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal around regulatory filing calendars, with public company reporting peaking shortly after each fiscal quarter end and mutual fund semi-annual and annual prospectus filings peaking in the second fiscal quarter.
quotes: The quarterly/annual public company reporting cycle subjects the Company to filing seasonality which peaks shortly after the end of each fiscal quarter.

Additionally, investment companies clients’ financial and regulatory reporting requirements include filings for mutual funds on a semi-annual basis as well as annual prospectus filings, which peaks during the second fiscal quarter.

business_model.claim: Software revenue growth is driven by client adoption, migration of traditional services onto platforms such as ActiveDisclosure (which grew approximately 24% in the third quarter of 2026), and Arc Suite price increases.
quotes: Software solutions net sales increased 5.0% versus the third quarter of 2025, driven by the continued momentum of ActiveDisclosure, a component of our compliance offerings, which grew approximately 24% as we continued to expand client adoption, increase the value of our offering, and migrate certain traditional services onto the platform.

Net sales of $128.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $12.3 million, or 10.6%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, due to higher non-TSR-related net sales of $6.5 million, largely driven by price increases, and higher net sales of $5.8 million from the Company’s TSR offering, primarily within ArcReporting and ArcDigital.

business_model.claim: Traditional CM-CCM and IC-CCM services generally lack long-term contracts, making client retention and referrals from investment banks, financial advisors, and law firms key revenue drivers.
quotes: The Company does not generally have long-term contracts for traditional services and products within the CM-CCM and IC-CCM segments and, therefore, relies on those clients’ continued use of DFIN’s services and products.
Although some of the Company’s software contracts are multi-year, both multi-year contracts and contracts that are less than one year are subject to renewals.

For instance, a portion of the Company’s net sales from capital markets clients is generated through referrals by investment banks, financial advisors and law firms that have utilized the Company’s services in connection with prior transactions.

business_model.claim: Low barriers to entry, industry fragmentation, client budget constraints, and emerging AI-enabled or self-filing competitors can pressure pricing and limit returns on AI product investments.
quotes: The financial communications services industry is highly competitive with relatively low barrier to entry and the industry remains highly fragmented in North America and internationally.
Management expects that competition will increase from existing competitors, as well as new and emerging entrants, including those offering AI-enabled or self-filing services and products.

Additionally, if clients are unwilling to pay sufficiently higher prices or separate fees for DFIN’s products that include AI capabilities or such capabilities do not fully address clients’ needs, the Company may not see a return on its investment.

business_model.claim: Consolidated cost of sales as a percentage of net sales and operating margins fluctuate with sales mix across higher- and lower-margin offerings, filing seasonality, and capital markets volatility.
quotes: The Company’s cost of sales as a percentage of net sales, consolidated income from operations, Segment Adjusted EBITDA and Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin may be affected by sales mix (i.e., a higher proportion of sales of higher or lower margin services or products relative to total sales).
Sales mix can vary period to period and is impacted by regulatory filing seasonality and global capital markets volatility.

business_model.claim: Cost of sales and SG&A expenses are driven by sales volumes, overhead cost allocations, and ongoing cost control initiatives.
quotes: The lower cost of sales is largely driven by lower sales volumes, cost control initiatives and lower overhead costs, whereas the lower SG&A expenses are primarily driven by cost control initiatives, lower bad debt expense of $6.5 million, lower overhead costs and lower incentive compensation expense, partially offset by higher share-based compensation expense of $6.2 million and higher healthcare expense of $2.3 million.

The increase in Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin was primarily due to higher software solutions and tech-enabled services net sales and cost control initiatives, partially offset by higher incentive compensation expense and higher selling expense as a result of the increase in sales volumes.

business_model.claim: DFIN directs substantially all of its capital expenditures budget to software development, which increases product development costs in software cost of sales and raises software amortization expense.
quotes: The Company continues to invest substantially all of its capital expenditures budget on software development, including for both investment companies and capital markets, most recently with the functionality developed in the new Venue platform, the Arc Suite for the Tailored Shareholder Reporting (“TSR”) regulations and the launch of cloud-based ActiveDisclosure and the ongoing development of additional features thereafter, including the ability to file transactional deals utilizing ActiveDisclosure.
Software solutions cost of sales increased primarily due to higher product development costs of $1.4 million and a lower allocation of overhead costs.

Depreciation and amortization of $59.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased $0.9 million, or 1.5%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to $2.8 million of accelerated amortization expense related to discontinued software recorded during the year ended December 31, 2024 and lower depreciation expense of $1.5 million, partially offset by higher software amortization expense of $3.4 million, driven by additional software development.

business_model.claim: Filing seasonality forces DFIN to hire temporary personnel, increase overtime/premium time, and outsource production during peak periods, although self-filing software reduces peak service-support needs.
quotes: The seasonality and associated operational implications include the need to increase staff during peak periods through a combined strategy of hiring temporary personnel, increasing the premium time of existing staff and outsourcing production for a number of services.

ActiveDisclosure and Arc Suite provide clients and their financial advisors software solutions which allow them to autonomously file and distribute compliance documents with regulatory agencies reducing the need for additional service support during peak periods.

business_model.claim: SG&A expenses are moved by selling expenses (which vary with sales volumes), incentive compensation, employee-related and healthcare costs, share-based compensation expense, and bad debt expense tied to client credit quality.
quotes: The increase in SG&A expenses was primarily driven by higher incentive compensation expense, higher selling expense and higher employee-related expense, partially offset by lower healthcare expense and lower bad debt expense of $1.0 million.
In addition, a weak economy could hinder the Company’s ability to collect amounts owed by clients.
Share-based compensation expense—Included charges of $31.4 million and $25.2 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

business_model.claim: Reliance on third-party data centers, cloud services, licensed software/hardware, and external engineers exposes costs to vendor price increases and project cost overruns, alongside ongoing cybersecurity prevention and remediation expenses.
quotes: The Company also relies on third parties for certain data center and cloud services to support services and product delivery to clients.
In addition, it is possible that the Company’s vendors could increase their prices, which could have an adverse impact on DFIN’s business, results of operations, financial position and cash flows.

The Company has incurred, and expects to continue to incur, expenses to prevent, investigate and remediate security breaches and vulnerabilities, including deploying additional personnel and protection technologies, training employees and engaging third-party experts and consultants.

business_model.claim: Reported expenses also reflect periodic restructuring and impairment charges—such as $6.1 million in employee termination costs and $3.9 million in software impairment in 2025—and the 2025 non-cash pension plan settlement charge of $82.8 million.
quotes: Restructuring, impairment and other charges, net—The year ended December 31, 2025 included employee termination costs of $6.1 million and $3.9 million of impairment charges related to software.

As a result of the Plan Settlement, the Company remeasured the Plan’s assets and obligations and recognized a non-cash settlement charge of $82.8 million during the year ended December 31, 2025, due to the recognition of unrealized accumulated Plan losses previously reported within accumulated other comprehensive loss on the audited Consolidated Balance Sheets.

competitive_position.claim: DFIN positions itself as a leading global provider of compliance and regulatory software and services serving public and private companies, mutual funds, and regulated investment firms.
quotes: DFIN is a leading global provider of compliance and regulatory software and services, supporting its clients’ complex capital markets transactions and essential financial reporting at every stage of the corporate lifecycle and fueling end-to-end investment company regulatory compliance needs.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1 Business (P1) and Item 1A Risk Factors (P2).
competitive_position.claim: In its Compliance and Communications Management segments, DFIN supports its market position through high-touch service delivery, around-the-clock transaction support, and referrals from financial institutions and law firms.
quotes: In its Compliance & Communications Management segments (CM-CCM and IC-CCM, as defined below), the Company’s strategy focuses on maintaining its market-leading position by offering a high-touch, service-oriented experience, using its unique combination of tech-enabled services and print and distribution capabilities.

The Company depends, in part, on the financial institutions, law firms and other third parties who use DFIN’s services and products to recommend solutions to their client base, which provides the Company the opportunity to reach a larger client base than it can reach through the direct sales and internal marketing efforts.

competitive_position.claim: DFIN differentiates its Venue, ActiveDisclosure, and Arc Suite software platforms through security certifications, annual third-party compliance audits, and embedded workflow tools such as auto-redaction, iXBRL tagging, and native Excel linking.
quotes: The Company’s Venue solution is a highly secure ISO/IEC 27001:2013-certified data room platform that allows clients to share confidential information in real-time throughout the transaction lifecycle.
ActiveDisclosure is ISO/IEC 27001:2013-certified, and the Company also engages third parties to perform annual SOC2 Type II compliance audits and penetration/vulnerability testing.

The Company’s Arc Suite software platform is ISO/IEC 27001:2013-certified and enables its investment companies clients to comply with applicable ongoing SEC, European and Canadian regulations as well as to create, manage and deliver accurate and timely financial communications to investors and regulators.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1 Business (P1) and 10-Q MD&A (P4).

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K MD&A (P3).

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A (P4) and Q3 2026 earnings release (P6).
growth_thesis.claim: In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total net sales grew $20.2 million, or 3.4%, to $614.7 million, supported by a $2.3 million increase in tech-enabled services net sales driven primarily by higher capital markets transactional volumes.
quotes: Net sales for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $20.2 million, or 3.4%, to $614.7 million from $594.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, including a $1.1 million, or 0.2%, increase due to changes in foreign currency exchange rates.
The increase in tech-enabled services net sales was primarily driven by higher transactional volumes, partially offset by lower compliance volumes.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A (P4) and Q3 2026 earnings release (P6).
growth_thesis.claim: Higher net sales, software mix, and ongoing operating efficiencies drove nine-month 2026 income from operations up $10.3 million, or 8.1%, to $137.1 million and lifted third-quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA margin by 120 basis points to 29.4%.
quotes: Income from operations for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $10.3 million, or 8.1%, to $137.1 million from $126.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to higher net sales of $20.2 million, as described above, and lower cost of sales of $2.2 million, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses of $11.9 million.
The combination of higher overall net sales and ongoing operating efficiencies expanded third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA margin to 29.4%, an increase of approximately 120 basis points year-over-year.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A (P4).
growth_thesis.claim: Evolving SEC disclosure rules requiring structured, machine-readable data and modern reporting formats accelerate DFIN’s client transition from print and distribution to software solutions.
quotes: Regulatory changes have enabled the Company to offer new value-added functionality and services, leverage its domain expertise and accelerate its transition from print and distribution to software solutions.

As the regulatory environment continues to evolve, regulators are also demanding a greater use of structured, machine-readable data in companies’ disclosures, more summary documents and layered website disclosures.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors (P2) and nine-month 2026 capital expenditure tables in the Q3 2026 earnings release (P6).
growth_thesis.claim: For software-led growth to continue, DFIN must attract new clients, expand use cases, and successfully release software enhancements funded by its $36.3 (table in millions) in nine-month 2026 capital expenditures that clients adopt and pay for, including AI-enabled features.
quotes: In order to accomplish this transition, the Company must attract new clients for those businesses and expand the addressable market and relevant use cases for its offerings.

The Company continues to invest substantially all of its capital expenditures budget on software development, including for both investment companies and capital markets, most recently with the functionality developed in the new Venue platform, the Arc Suite for the Tailored Shareholder Reporting (“TSR”) regulations and the launch of cloud-based ActiveDisclosure and the ongoing development of additional features thereafter, including the ability to file transactional deals utilizing ActiveDisclosure.

Additionally, if clients are unwilling to pay sufficiently higher prices or separate fees for DFIN’s products that include AI capabilities or such capabilities do not fully address clients’ needs, the Company may not see a return on its investment.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors (P2).
growth_thesis.claim: Continued growth requires sustaining client retention and renewals across both multi-year and sub-one-year software contracts, alongside ongoing client referrals from investment banks, financial advisors, and law firms.
quotes: Although some of the Company’s software contracts are multi-year, both multi-year contracts and contracts that are less than one year are subject to renewals.

The Company does not generally have long-term contracts for traditional services and products within the CM-CCM and IC-CCM segments and, therefore, relies on those clients’ continued use of DFIN’s services and products.

For instance, a portion of the Company’s net sales from capital markets clients is generated through referrals by investment banks, financial advisors and law firms that have utilized the Company’s services in connection with prior transactions.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors (P2) and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A (P4).
growth_thesis.claim: For capital markets transactional and Venue growth to continue, global IPO, M&A, and debt-offering activity must remain healthy without severe macroeconomic downturns, market volatility, or U.S. federal government shutdowns.
quotes: As a result, a significant portion of the Company’s business is dependent on the global market for IPOs, secondary offerings, M&A, public and private debt offerings, leveraged buyouts, spinouts, SPAC and de-SPAC transactions and other similar transactions.
Recently, U.S. capital markets transactions, especially IPO and M&A transactions were disrupted by the U.S. federal government shutdown that occurred during the fourth quarter of 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors (P2).
growth_thesis.claim: Sustaining client trust and platform adoption requires maintaining cybersecurity, system availability, and uninterrupted third-party cloud, data center, and licensed software services.
quotes: Maintaining the confidentiality, integrity and availability of DFIN’s systems, software and solutions is an issue of critical importance for the Company and its clients and users who rely on DFIN’s systems to prepare regulatory filings and store and exchange large volumes of information, much of which is proprietary, confidential and may constitute material nonpublic information.
The Company also relies on third parties for certain data center and cloud services to support services and product delivery to clients.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors (P2).

quotes: Management expects that competition will increase from existing competitors, as well as new and emerging entrants, including those offering AI-enabled or self-filing services and products.
Budgetary constraints or other economic pressures on the Company’s existing or potential clients may impact DFIN’s ability to price its services and products profitably.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors (P2).
growth_thesis.claim: Delivering product upgrades and high-touch service margins requires hiring and retaining experienced software engineers, senior sales executives, and financial reporting professionals.
quotes: Competition for these individuals is intense, especially for engineers with high levels of experience in designing and developing software and internet-related services, senior sales executives and professional services personnel with appropriate financial reporting experience.
A high level of customer support is critical for the successful marketing, sale and retention of DFIN’s solutions.

material_events.claim: DFIN amended its primary defined benefit plan in August 2024 to terminate it and settled the plan obligations during the year ended December 31, 2025 via lump sum payments and a non-participating irrevocable group annuity contract, making an $11.3 million net cash contribution and recognizing an $82.8 million non-cash settlement charge.
quotes: In August 2024, the Company executed an amendment to commence the process of terminating the Company’s primary defined benefit plan (the “Plan”).

During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company settled the Plan obligations through a combination of lump sum payments to certain Plan participants and the purchase of a non-participating irrevocable group annuity contract (the “Plan Settlement”).
In connection with the Plan Settlement, the Company made an $11.3 million, net cash contribution to fully fund the Plan.

As a result of the Plan Settlement, the Company remeasured the Plan’s assets and obligations and recognized a non-cash settlement charge of $82.8 million during the year ended December 31, 2025, due to the recognition of unrealized accumulated Plan losses previously reported within accumulated other comprehensive loss on the audited Consolidated Balance Sheets.

risks.claim: Client migration away from physical print and traditional compliance services reduced Print and distribution net sales by 16.1% and Tech-enabled services net sales by 7.0% in 2025.
quotes: The prevailing trend is toward clients choosing to utilize the Company’s software solutions, in conjunction with its tech-enabled services, to meet their document and filing needs, while at the same time shifting away from physical print and distribution of documents, except for when it is still regulatorily required or requested by clients.
Net sales of print and distribution of $110.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased $21.1 million, or 16.1%, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.
Software solutions net sales of $95.2 million, an increase of 5.0% from the third quarter of 2025; Software solutions net sales accounted for 51.5% of total net sales.

risks.claim: DFIN’s systems store material nonpublic information about public reporting companies and M&A transactions, making it an ongoing target for cyberattacks and data leaks.
quotes: Given DFIN’s systems contain material nonpublic information about public reporting companies and potential M&A activities prior to its public release, the Company has been, and expects it will continue to be, a target of hacking or cybercrime.
There is no guarantee that these measures will be adequate to safeguard against all data security breaches, system compromises or misuses of data.
ActiveDisclosure is ISO/IEC 27001:2013-certified, and the Company also engages third parties to perform annual SOC2 Type II compliance audits and penetration/vulnerability testing.

The Company continues to invest substantially all of its capital expenditures budget on software development, including for both investment companies and capital markets, most recently with the functionality developed in the new Venue platform, the Arc Suite for the Tailored Shareholder Reporting (“TSR”) regulations and the launch of cloud-based ActiveDisclosure and the ongoing development of additional features thereafter, including the ability to file transactional deals utilizing ActiveDisclosure.

quotes: The financial communications services industry is highly competitive with relatively low barrier to entry and the industry remains highly fragmented in North America and internationally.
Budgetary constraints or other economic pressures on the Company’s existing or potential clients may impact DFIN’s ability to price its services and products profitably.

Segment Adjusted EBITDA margin increased by approximately 500 bps from 34.2% for the year ended December 31, 2024 to 39.2% for the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily due to an approximately 370 bps and 130 bps decrease in SG&A expenses and cost of sales as a percentage of net sales, respectively, largely driven by price increases.

risks.claim: DFIN relies on third-party cloud, data center, software, and engineering contractor resources whose outages, price increases, bugs, or contract losses could disrupt service delivery.
quotes: The Company also relies on third parties for certain data center and cloud services to support services and product delivery to clients.

Any loss of the right to use any of these systems and services could result in delays in the provisioning of DFIN’s services, which could negatively affect the Company’s business until alternatives are either developed by the Company or identified, obtained and integrated.
The Company has disaster recovery and business continuity plans in place in the event of system failure due to any of these events and these plans are tested regularly.

The Company utilizes product pilots, alpha release and other means to gauge market demand as DFIN’s operating results would suffer if its innovations are not responsive to the needs of the Company’s clients, are not appropriately timed with market opportunities or are not brought to market effectively.
